source_text: Idcirco igitur, quoniam septenario numero dierum et coelestia et terrestria reguntur, principii loco, de hac septimam ad omnium septimanarium rigionum metibor, et prout potuero, virtutis diem in eam consummationem conabor exprimere. In principio fecit Deus lucem, eamque duodenario mero horarum, die noctuque, divisit, idcirco videlicet, ut laboribus hominum requies locum noctem dies superduceret, rursus dies supervinceret; hac se alterna vice labor quetis refoveretur, quies exercitatione rursus diei temperaretur. Quarto die fecit duo luminaria in coelo, majus et minus, ut alterum praeesset diei, alterum nocti, solis et lunae; caeteraque sidera posuit in coelo, ut lucerent super terram, et discernerent tempora et annos et menses et dies et horas per stationes. Nunc ratio veritatis ostenditur, quare dies IIII, tetras nuncupatur; quare usque ad horam nonam jejunamus , usque ad vesperam, aut superpositio usque in alterum diem fiat. Mundus itaque iste ex quatuor elementis constat, igne, aqua, coelo, terra. Haec igitur quator elementa temporum tetradem faciunt. Sol quoque et luna per anni spatium quatuor tempora efficiunt, veris, aestatis, autumni, hyemis; et haec tempora tetradem faciunt. Et ut ex ea re longius enarrem, ecce quatuor animalia ante thronum Dei. quatuor evangelia, quatuor flumina in paradiso fluentia, quatuor generationes populorum, ab Adam usque ad Noe, a Noe usque ad Abraham, ab Abraham usque ad Moysem, a Moyse usque ad Christum Dominum, Filium Dei; et quatuor animalia hominis, vituli, leonis, aquilae; et quatuor flumina, Fyson, Geon, Tygris, Euphrates. Homo Christus Jesus auctor eorum, quae supra memoravimus, tetrade ab impiis comprehensus est. Itaque ob captivitatem ejus tetradem ob majestatem operum suorum, et tempora humanitatis salubria, frugibus laeta, tempestatibus tranquilla, decurrant, ideo aut superpositionem facimus. Die quinto terra et aqua foetus suos ediderunt. Die sexto creata sunt, quae deerant; ac sic Deus hominem de humo instruxit, dominum omnium rerum, quae super terram et super aquam creavit. Prius tamen angelos atque archangelos creavit, quam hominem finxit, spiritalia terrenis anteponens. Prius enim lux, quam coelum et terram. Hic dies sextus parasceve appellatur, praeparatio scilicet regni; Adam enim quem ad imaginem et similitudinem suam consummavit.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, because the number seven of days rules both heavenly and earthly things, in the place of a beginning, I will measure from this seventh to all septenary regions, and as much as I can, I will try to express the day of virtue to its consummation. In the beginning, God made light, and He divided it by a twelve-hour measure of hours, day and night, therefore, so that rest might take the place of labor for men by night, and day might overcome it again; thus labor is restored by alternating rest, and rest is tempered by the exercise of day again. On the fourth day, He made two luminaries in the heaven, a greater and a lesser one, so that one might preside over the day, the other over the night, the sun and the moon; and He placed the other stars in the heaven, so that they might shine over the earth, and distinguish times and years and months and days and hours by their stations. Now the reason of truth is shown, why the fourth day is called tetras; why we fast until the ninth hour, until evening, or a superposition is made until the next day. This world, therefore, consists of four elements, fire, water, heaven, earth. These four elements, therefore, make a tetrad of times. The sun and the moon also make four times through the space of a year, spring, summer, autumn, winter; and these times make a tetrad. And that I might speak more fully from this thing, behold, four living creatures before the throne of God, four Gospels, four rivers flowing in paradise, four generations of peoples, from Adam to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, from Moses to Christ the Lord, the Son of God; and four living creatures of man, the calf, the lion, the eagle; and four rivers, Fyson, Geon, Tygris, Euphrates. Christ Jesus, the author of those things which we mentioned above, was seized by the tetrad of the impious. Therefore, on account of His captivity, we make a tetrad, on account of the majesty of His works, and the healthy times of humanity, joyful with fruits, tranquil with storms, run their course, therefore we make a superposition. On the fifth day, the earth and water brought forth their offspring. On the sixth day, those things which were lacking were created; and thus God formed man from the earth, the lord of all things which He created over the earth and over the water. Nevertheless, He created angels and archangels before He formed man, preferring spiritual things to earthly ones. For light was before heaven and earth. This sixth day is called parasceve, that is, a preparation of the kingdom; for Adam, whom He consummated in His own image and likeness.

pass_b_english: Because a seven‑day cycle governs both heavenly and earthly things, I take this seventh day as my starting point and, as far as I am able, I will measure from it to every septenary region and try to set forth the day of virtue to its consummation.

In the beginning God made light (Genesis 1:3), and He divided it into a twelve‑hour measure of day and night so that night might give rest a place after human labor, and day might overcome night again; thus labor is refreshed by alternating rest, and rest is tempered by the exercise of day.

On the fourth day He made two luminaries in the heavens, a greater and a lesser, that one might preside over the day and the other over the night—the sun and the moon (Genesis 1:14-19)—and He set the other stars in the heavens to shine on the earth and to mark off seasons, years, months, days, and hours by their courses.
Now the reason of truth is shown: why the fourth day is called tetras, why we fast until the ninth hour, until evening, or why a superposition is kept until the next day.
This world consists of four elements—fire, water, heaven, earth—and these four elements make a tetrad of times.
The sun and the moon also produce four seasons through the course of a year—spring, summer, autumn, winter—and those seasons make a tetrad.

To speak more fully from this point: behold, four living creatures before the throne of God (Revelation 4:6-8), four Gospels, four rivers flowing in paradise, four generations of peoples from Adam to Noah, from Noah to Abraham, from Abraham to Moses, from Moses to Christ the Lord, the Son of God; and four living creatures of man—the calf, the lion, the eagle; and four rivers—Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates.
Christ Jesus, the author of the things mentioned above, was seized by the tetrad of the impious.

Therefore, because of His captivity, we observe a tetrad; because of the majesty of His works, and because the wholesome times of humanity, joyful with fruits and tranquil with seasons, run their course, we make a superposition.
On the fifth day the earth and water brought forth their offspring.
On the sixth day the things that were still lacking were created; and so God formed man from the dust, the lord of all things that He had created on the earth and in the water (Genesis 2:2-3).
Nevertheless, He created angels and archangels before He formed man, preferring spiritual things to earthly ones, for light existed before heaven and earth.
This sixth day is called Parasceve, that is, a preparation of the kingdom; for Adam was completed in God's own image and likeness.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required scripture citations (Genesis 1:3, Genesis 1:14-19, Revelation 4:6-8, Genesis 2:2-3) which were alluded to in the Latin. The translation of 'Fyson, Geon, Tygris, Euphrates' as 'Pishon, Gihon, Tigris, Euphrates' is a standard and correct English rendering of the biblical names. The distinction between 'spiritual things' and 'earthly ones' is preserved.
